Name of the Surah

• It is called Al-Furqan (the Criterion), because it opens with mention of the Furqan, which is the Qur'an that distinguishes between truth and falsehood.

Some of the Surah's Objectives

• Exalting the Qur'an and what it contains of guidance, and subtly reminding people of the favour of being guided by it; exalting the Messenger ﷺ to whom the Qur'an was sent down, mentioning the proofs of his truthfulness and his elevation above the worldly desires, and that he follows the same path as the other Messengers; this is to strengthen the Messenger ﷺ in his call and to console him over the opposition of his people.

• Affirming the Resurrection, giving glad tidings of reward to the righteous in the Hereafter, warning the polytheists of punishment, explaining the humiliation that will befall them on the Day of Resurrection, and the regret and anguish that will result from their denial of the Messenger ﷺ, their associating partners with Allah, and their following of the people of misguidance.

• Presenting evidence for the Oneness of Allah, the Exalted, by mentioning a number of the marvels of His creation in this universe, such as its changes and cosmic phenomena, and the creation of man; and declaring Him far above having a son or a partner; and refuting the divinity of idols and the claims that the angels are daughters of Allah, glorified and exalted is He.

• Explaining the attributes of the servants of the Most Merciful, whom Allah has singled out with praiseworthy character and steadfastness in this life upon the Sharia, and mentioning the great reward Allah has prepared for them in the Gardens of Bliss, and an allusion to a near punishment that will befall the deniers.

[Tafsir]

Blessed is Allah; His bounties are great and abundant, and His attributes are perfect, glorified and exalted is He, who sent down the Furqan, the Qur'an that distinguishes between truth and falsehood, upon His servant Muhammad ﷺ, so that he may be a messenger to mankind and the jinn, warning them of the punishment of Allah.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 25, verse 2:

He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, who has not taken a son, and who has no partner in His dominion; and He is the One who created everything and proportioned it according to what suits it of creation, in accordance with what His wisdom requires, without deficiency or defect.

The polytheists of the Arabs took deities besides Allah that cannot create anything, while Allah created them and created those who worship them. They cannot ward off harm from themselves or bring about benefit for themselves, and they cannot cause a living being to die or bring a dead one to life, or raise any of the dead from their graves alive.

And those who disbelieve in Allah say: "This Qur'an is nothing but a lie and a fabrication, which Muhammad has invented, and other people have helped him with it." They have committed a monstrous wrong and uttered a grievous falsehood. The Qur'an is not something that any human being could invent.
They said about the Qur'an: "It is the fables of the ancients, which were written down in their books, and Muhammad has had them copied. They are read to him morning and evening."

Say, O Messenger, to these disbelievers: Indeed, the One who sent down the Qur'an is Allah, whose knowledge encompasses what is in the heavens and the earth. Indeed, He is ever Oft-Forgiving to those who repent from sins and disobedience, and Merciful to them, in that He does not hasten to punish them.

The polytheists said: "What is wrong with this man who claims to be a messenger of God?" - they mean Muhammad (ﷺ) - "He eats food like us and walks in the markets to seek provision. Why has God not sent an angel with him to bear witness to his truthfulness, or why has a treasure of wealth not been sent down to him from heaven, or why does he not have a great garden from whose fruit he may eat?" And these wrongdoers who denied said: "You are following nothing but a man afflicted by sorcery, whose mind has been overcome."

Consider, O Messenger, how the deniers have spoken about you these strange statements, which, because of their oddity, resemble mere parables, in order to reach their denial of you. Thus they have strayed far from the truth, so they find no way to it, by which they might substantiate what they have said about you of falsehood and fabrication.

Exalted are the blessings of Allah, and abundant is His goodness, He who, if He wills, will grant you, O Messenger, better than what they wished for you: He will give you in this world gardens abundant with rivers flowing through them, and He will give you grand palaces therein.

The passage is a short tafsir of Qur'an 25:11. Translating faithfully:

They did not deny you because you eat food and walk in the markets. Rather, they denied the Day of Resurrection and what it contains of recompense. And We have prepared a blazing, fierce Fire for those who deny the Hour, its fuel being them.
When the Fire sees these deniers on the Day of Resurrection from a distant place, they will hear its boiling and its roaring, from its intense rage against them.
And when they are thrown into a narrow place of Hellfire, their hands bound together with chains to their necks, they will cry out for destruction upon themselves, seeking deliverance from it.
It is said to them, to despair them: "Do not call out for destruction today just once, but call for it many times; that will only increase your distress, for there is no deliverance for you."

Say (to them), O Messenger: "Is that (Fire) better, or the Garden of eternal bliss that has been promised to those who fear their Lord? It is a reward for their deeds and a final destination to which they will return in the Hereafter."

For these obedient ones there is in Paradise whatever they desire of the delights of bliss; their enjoyment therein is lasting. Their entry into it was, O Messenger, a promise from your Lord that was requested (in prayer), which the righteous servants of Allah ask for, and Allah does not break His promise.

On the Day of Resurrection, Allah will gather the polytheists together with those they used to worship besides Him. He will say to those deities: "Did you lead these servants of Mine astray from the path of truth, and command them to worship you? Or did they themselves go astray from the way, so that they worshipped you of their own accord?"

The worshipped beings besides God will say: "Glory be to You, our Lord! It was not right for us to take anyone besides You as protectors whom we would befriend. But You gave these polytheists and their fathers enjoyment through wealth and well-being in this world, until they forgot Your remembrance and associated others with You, and they were a people doomed to destruction, overcome by wretchedness and abandonment."

Then it will be said to the polytheists: "Indeed, those whom you worshipped have denied what you claimed about them. So here you are, unable to avert the punishment from yourselves or to help yourselves. And whoever sets up partners with God, wronging himself by worshipping other than God and dying in that state, God will punish him with a severe punishment."

The Noble Qur'an Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on Surah 25, verse 20:

We did not send before you, O Messenger, any of Our messengers except that they were human beings who ate food and walked in the markets. Those who do not expect to meet Us (لا يؤمِّلون لقاء ربهم) after their death, because of their denial of it, said: "Why have the angels not been sent down to us, to tell us that Muhammad is truthful? We came to what they had done of works of goodness and piety, and rendered it worthless dust, of no benefit to them, like scattered dust motes, which are the fine specks of dust seen in the sunlight. That is because a deed benefits no one in the Hereafter unless its doer possesses: faith in Allah, sincerity toward Him, and following His Messenger Muhammad (ﷺ).

The people of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection are better in their abode than the people of the Fire, and finer in their dwelling places in Paradise. Their rest is complete, and their bliss is not mixed with any distress.

Remember, O Messenger, that Day when the sky will split open, and white, thin clouds will appear through its openings, and Allah will send down the angels of the heavens on that Day, and they will surround the creation at the place of gathering. The true sovereignty on that Day belongs to the Most Merciful alone, to the exclusion of anyone else. And that Day will be difficult and severe for the disbelievers, because of the punishment and painful torment they will receive.

And just as We have made for you, O Messenger, enemies from among the criminals of your people, We have made for every prophet among the prophets an enemy from among the criminals of his people. So be patient, as they were patient. And your Lord is sufficient as a guide, a director, and a helper who will support you against your enemies. In this is consolation for His Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ).

The disbelievers said: "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to Muhammad all at once, like the Torah, the Gospel and the Psalms?" Allah, glorified and exalted, said: "Thus We sent it down in parts, so that We might strengthen your heart with it and increase your tranquility, that you may understand it and retain it. Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 25, verse 44:

**Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 25, verse 56:**

And We did not send you, O Messenger, except as a bringer of good news to the believers of Paradise and a warner to the disbelievers of the Fire.

Say to them: I do not ask of you any reward for conveying the message, but whoever wishes to be guided and to take the path of truth to his Lord, and to spend in pursuit of His pleasure, (may do so). I do not compel you to it, but it is good for your own selves.

And put your trust in Allah, the Ever-Living who possesses all the perfect attributes of life, as befits His majesty, the One who never dies, and glorify Him, exalting Him above all attributes of deficiency. And sufficient is Allah as One Who is Aware of the sins of His creatures; nothing of them is hidden from Him, and He will call them to account for them and recompense them for them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 25, verse 59:

He is the One who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days, then established Himself (istawa, "rose above and ascended") upon the Throne in a manner befitting His majesty. He is the Most Merciful, so ask about Him, O Prophet, one who is well-informed. By this He, glorified is He, means His own noble Self, for He is the One who knows His attributes, His greatness, and His majesty. No one among mankind knows Allah better or informs about Him more than His servant and Messenger, Muhammad (ﷺ).

When it is said to the disbelievers, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful (al-Rahman) and worship Him," they say, "We do not know the Most Merciful. Shall we prostrate to what you command us to prostrate to, out of obedience to your order?" Their being called to prostrate to the Most Merciful only increased them in distance from faith and in aversion to it.

Commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 25, verse 61:

The blessings of the Most Merciful are great, and His goodness is abundant. He who placed in the sky the great stars in their stations, and placed in it a sun that gives light and a moon that gives illumination.

And He it is who made the night and the day succeed each other, one following the other, for whoever wishes to take heed through this and believe in the Governor, the Creator, or wishes to give thanks to Allah, the Exalted, for His blessings and favours.

And the righteous servants of the Most Merciful (ʿIbad al-Rahman) walk upon the earth with tranquility, humble. When the ignorant and foolish address them with harm, they answer them with good speech (al-maʿruf min al-qawl), and they address them with words by which they are kept safe from sin, and from meeting ignorance with ignorance.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 25, verses 68–71:

Those who devote worship solely to God, and do not invoke or worship any deity besides Him, and do not kill the soul which God has forbidden to be killed, except for a just cause: [such as] apostasy after belief, or adultery after marriage, or killing a soul unjustly. And they do not commit adultery; rather, they guard their private parts, except with their spouses or what their right hands possess. Whoever commits any of these major sins will meet a punishment in the Hereafter. ﴿His punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein in humiliation and disgrace.﴾ (The threat of eternal abiding applies to whoever commits all of them, or to whoever associates partners with God.) But whoever repents from these sins with sincere repentance, believes with firm faith combined with righteous deeds, those are the ones whose evil deeds God will erase and replace with good deeds, because of their repentance and remorse. God is Forgiving to whoever repents and Merciful to His servants, in that He called them to repentance after they had defied Him with the greatest of sins. And whoever repents from the sins he committed and does righteous deeds, he thereby returns to God with a true return, so God accepts his repentance and expiates his sins.

Those who are characterized by the attributes mentioned earlier, the servants of the Most Merciful, will be rewarded with the highest ranks of Paradise, by the mercy of God and because of their patience in obedience. They will be greeted in Paradise with salutations and peace from the angels, and with a good life and safety from afflictions, abiding therein forever without death. How good a place of settling and a station in which to dwell it is, and they will not desire any change from it.

God, exalted is He, informs that He does not care for or attend to people were it not for their calling upon Him, both the calling of worship and the calling of petition. "You have indeed denied"—O disbelievers—"so your denial will lead to a punishment that will cling to you as a creditor clings to his debtor, and it will destroy you in this world and in the Hereafter."
